I would immediately call for help, ask an assistant to note the time, ask the woman to stop pushing temporarily, avoid excessive traction and fundal pressure, and proceed systematically with McRoberts manoeuvre followed by suprapubic pressure and, if unsuccessful, internal manoeuvres including delivery of the posterior arm and rotational manoeuvres.”

“Shoulder dystocia was recognized immediately. Help was called and the time of head delivery documented. The neonate was immediately assessed by the neonatal team. I would now assess maternal blood loss and genital tract trauma, document the sequence of events and arrange appropriate maternal and neonatal follow-up.”

blocks.text: “I would recognize this as an obstetric emergency because the fetal head has delivered but the shoulders have failed to deliver with routine gentle axial traction. I would immediately call for senior obstetric, midwifery and neonatal assistance and ask someone to document the time of head delivery.

I would ask the woman to stop pushing temporarily, avoid excessive traction on the fetal head and avoid fundal pressure. I would perform McRoberts manoeuvre and apply suprapubic pressure. If these are unsuccessful, I would consider an episiotomy if additional access is required and proceed systematically to internal rotational manoeuvres and delivery of the posterior arm. If necessary, I would turn the woman onto all fours.

If the dystocia remains unresolved, I would escalate to experienced senior obstetric management and consider advanced rescue manoeuvres. Once the baby is delivered, I would prioritize neonatal resuscitation and assessment for brachial plexus injury and fractures, while assessing the mother for postpartum haemorrhage and genital tract trauma. I would ensure comprehensive documentation and debrief the woman and her birth partner afterwards.”

“Shoulder dystocia — call for help, stop excessive traction and fundal pressure, McRoberts, suprapubic pressure, internal manoeuvres/posterior arm, all fours, escalate if unresolved, then assess baby and mother and document.”
That is the sequence you should be able to reproduce under pressure.
